neighbours.label: civilian-sector adjective (commercial, civil, domestic) modifying a noun in security, defence or space text, the non-military side of a military/civilian distinction
fire: The rocket will carry two commercial satellites along with a spy payload.
After the attacks, civil aviation was grounded across the country for days.
The bureau was accused of wiretapping domestic political groups during the war.
Officials said the reactor would only produce medical isotopes, not weapons fuel.
The new port will serve commercial shipping as well as the navy.
Investigators believe the hijackers trained on commercial flight simulators.
The spy agency was barred from collecting data on domestic targets.
The airport handles civil traffic alongside a small air force wing.
quiet: The rocket will carry two classified satellites along with a spy payload.
After the attacks, air force patrols were increased across the country for days.
The bureau was accused of wiretapping foreign intelligence officers during the war.
Officials said the reactor would only produce small amounts of fuel, not weapons.
The new port will serve the navy and its submarines.
Investigators believe the hijackers trained for months in the desert.
The spy agency was barred from collecting data on allied governments.
The airport handles military traffic for a small air force wing.

notes: Card: ' commercial' x5, ' domestic' x5, ' economic', ' medical', ' civil'; + pole is NATO/military bases. Probe: 'military airliner' also fired 0.33, so this may fail.
